note: al-Nadwī's Sīra (al-sira-al-nabawiyya-nadwi, chapters 101–106): every contradiction tools/grammar_audit.js listed on the new package, judged by the line. The first run listed 15; five were the author's (the clause line of «وَسَلَّمَ» in the prayer after the Prophet's name said «conjoined to صَلَّى» where Qawāʿid al-Iʿrāb names a clause conjoined to a muʿtariḍa as part of the muʿtariḍa with no seat) and the kit's line was corrected (listed under «corrected»). Second run: 10 records, all judged here: E = the engine is wrong by the books. One record is an older line (talkhis-al-miftah 14:s4:2) that the case engine reads differently once the Sīra is on the shelf; judged E, the authored line unchanged. Instalment 2 (chapters 107–112): the audit listed 18 new records on the package, judged here (15 E, 2 C, 1 undecided — «وأنّه», listed for the hoca); none was the author's.

records.why: «يَوْمَ الْإِثْنَيْنِ»: the day-name الِاثْنَانِ is treated as the dual (it is listed among what is joined to the dual, مُلْحَقٌ بِالْمُثَنَّى — al-Ashmūnī on the Alfiyya, bāb al-muʿrab); as a muḍāf ilayh it is in jarr by the yāʾ. The engine reads it as a sound singular with kasra.
«الِانْتِبَاه» is a sound singular maṣdar (Form VII of ن ب ه) in jarr by the kasra after the lām of taqwiya; the engine reads its final «ـاه» as a dual whose nūn dropped — there is no dual here.
«مِنْ أَبِي الصَّبِيِّ»: أَبُو is annexed to الصَّبِيّ (not to the speaker's yāʾ), one of the five nouns, in jarr by the yāʾ (al-Ājurrūmiyya, signs of jarr). The engine reads «أَبِي» as «my father».

«بُحَيْرَةُ سَاوَا»: سَاوَا is a foreign place-name (the print's spelling of Sāwa), barred from tanwin (ʿalamiyya + ʿujma / taʾnīth), its sign estimated on the final alif; a proper name of a place takes no tanwin here — the engine's «سَاوًا» treats it as an indefinite common noun.

«الَّتِي اشْتَهَرَ بِهَا بَنُو سَعْدٍ»: بَنُو is the doer of اشْتَهَرَ (اشْتَهَرَ is intransitive; بِهَا is its jarr complement and the ṣila's link), in rafʿ by the waw; nothing in the clause can make it an object.

«يَوْمَ الْإِثْنَيْنِ» hangs on «وُلِدَ»: «صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ» is a parenthetical prayer with no seat (Qawāʿid al-Iʿrāb, al-muʿtariḍa), and nothing in a muʿtariḍa governs what lies outside it. The engine takes the nearest verb.
«عَامَ الْفِيلِ» is a second adverb of time on «وُلِدَ» (the year of the birth), not something hanging on the month-name «رَبِيعٍ» — a proper name of a month is no governor of a ẓarf.
«لَمَّا» (the ḥīniyya ẓarf with the sense of a condition) hangs on its answer «أَرْسَلَتْ» (Mughnī, lammā; Qawāʿid bāb 2); «صَلَّى» belongs to the parenthetical prayer and governs nothing outside it.
«مَعَ إِخْوَتِهِ» hangs on «رَعَى»; «وَسَلَّمَ» closes the parenthetical prayer and governs nothing outside it.

«فِيمَا بَعْدُ»: «مَا» is a relative noun in jarr after «فِي» (the phrase hangs on «يَقُولُ»); «بَعْدُ» — built on ḍamm, its annexation cut off — is the ṣila, hanging on an omitted «اسْتَقَرَّ». To hang بَعْدُ on يَقُولُ would leave مَا without a ṣila.

An OLDER line the new corpus moved (not edited): «مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ» (al-Fātiḥa 1:4) — «يَوْمِ» is the muḍāf ilayh of «مَالِكِ», in jarr; the engine now offers the ẓarf «يَوْمَ» because the Sīra twice writes «يَوْمَ …» as an adverb of time. The Qurʾān's reading stands.
«حِينَذَاكَ» is حِينَ, an adverb of time in nasb by the fatha, annexed to the demonstrative ذَاكَ; there is no dual here — the engine reads the final «ـاك» as a dual sign.
«أَنَّ أَبَا رَسُولِ اللهِ … عَبْدَ اللهِ بْنَ عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ»: عَبْدَ is the badal of أَبَا (nasb), so its adjective بْنَ is in nasb; the engine follows the nearest jarr word «اللهِ».
«قَبْرَ بَعْلِهَا الْحَبِيبِ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ …»: عَبْدِ is the badal of بَعْلِهَا (jarr), so بْنِ is in jarr; the engine's «بْنَ» has no governor.
«فَتَعَلَّقَ بِعَمِّهِ»: بِ + عَمِّ (paternal uncle) + هِ, a noun in jarr; the engine reads a past verb «عَمَّهُ».
«لَمَّا» hangs on its answer «خَرَجَتْ»; «صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ» is a parenthetical prayer with no seat (Qawāʿid al-Iʿrāb, al-muʿtariḍa); nothing inside it governs what lies outside.
«وَذٰلِكَ الشَّأْنُ مَعَهُ»: the adverb is the predicate of the nominal clause; it cannot hang on «الْحَنُونِ», an adjective inside the preceding clause.
«لَمَّا» hangs on its answer «مَاتَ»; «صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ» is a parenthetical prayer with no seat (Qawāʿid al-Iʿrāb, al-muʿtariḍa); nothing inside it governs what lies outside.
«وَالْفَرْقُ بَيْنَهُمَا وَاضِحٌ» is a new nominal clause; «بَيْنَهُمَا» belongs to it (a hal of الْفَرْقُ, or on its predicate), not to «تَجْرِيبِيًّا» of the clause before.

«بَعْدَ عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ» hangs on the omitted predicate of كَانَ; «صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ» is a parenthetical prayer with no seat (Qawāʿid al-Iʿrāb, al-muʿtariḍa); nothing inside it governs what lies outside.

«مَعَ عَمِّهِ» is the predicate of كَانَ (on its omitted «كَائِنًا»); «صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ» is a parenthetical prayer with no seat (Qawāʿid al-Iʿrāb, al-muʿtariḍa); nothing inside it governs what lies outside.
«لَمَّا» hangs on its answer «اهْتَمَّ»; «يُقَالُ» belongs to the adjective clause of «رَاهِبٌ» inside the lammā clause.
«لَمَّا» hangs on its answer «احْتَفَى»; «صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ» is a parenthetical prayer with no seat (Qawāʿid al-Iʿrāb, al-muʿtariḍa); nothing inside it governs what lies outside.
«مَعَ بِلَالٍ» hangs on «أَرْسَلَ»; «صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ» is a parenthetical prayer with no seat (Qawāʿid al-Iʿrāb, al-muʿtariḍa); nothing inside it governs what lies outside.
«مَعَ تَوَفُّرِ هِمَمِهِمْ» may hang on «حَكَتْهُ» (they did not tell it despite …) or, as the line says, on an omitted hal of «الْأَشْيَاخُ»; the sense is the same.

cite.ar: كدأبك: جار ومجرور، قيل: متعلقان بقوله (قفا نبك) وقيل: الكاف اسم بمعنى

records.why: «قَدْ جَاءَ فِي … أَنَّ جَمِيعَ رِوَايَاتِ …»: the أَنَّ clause is the doer of «جَاءَ», so its hamza takes fatha (Shudhūr, mawāḍiʿ fatḥ anna); it does not open a sentence.

«وَوَقَعَ فِي كِتَابِ التِّرْمِذِيِّ … أَنَّهُ بَعَثَ»: the أَنَّ clause is the doer of «وَقَعَ» → fatha; «قَالَ» stands in the sentence before, and its quotation opens with «وَوَقَعَ», not with أَنَّ.

«وأنّه مِنَ الْغَلَطِ الْوَاضِحِ»: the sense (Ibn al-Qayyim's own judgement, «وهو من الغلط» in Zād al-Maʿād) wants a new clause, «وَإِنَّهُ»; the print writes the hamza above the alif («وأنّه»), so the line keeps the print and reads it conjoined; listed for the hoca.

«فَإِنَّهُ كَائِنٌ لِابْنِ أَخِيكَ هٰذَا شَأْنٌ عَظِيمٌ»: the hāʾ is the pronoun of the matter whose predicate is the clause; its mubtadaʾ «شَأْنٌ» is a nakira made definite enough by its adjective «عَظِيمٌ», so the single-word predicate «كَائِنٌ» may go first; another reading makes «كَائِنٌ» the participle of defective kāna with «شَأْنٌ» its noun. Listed for the hoca.
